note: Kinds are not added together. Only rows with counts yes enter a firm total.

rows.counterparty: State Grid / local wind and solar
rows.headline: Alibaba runs Zhangbei data centers on wind and solar
rows.summary: Alibaba Cloud's Zhangbei data center cluster in Hebei is sited in a wind and solar resource zone and uses natural free-cooling plus local renewables, an early model for green hyperscale compute in China.

rows.headline: Chindata commits to 100 percent renewable energy
rows.summary: Chindata Group pledged to power its hyperscale campuses with 100 percent renewable energy and reach carbon neutrality by 2030, among the first net-zero commitments from a Chinese data center operator.

rows.headline: Google and Fervo launch first corporate geothermal deal
rows.summary: Google partnered with Fervo Energy on Project Red, the first corporate agreement to develop an enhanced geothermal system. The 3.5 MW pilot in northern Nevada's Blue Mountain field began delivering carbon-free power to the local grid serving Google's Nevada data centers in 2023, becoming the longest-running enhanced geothermal system at the time.

rows.headline: Baidu targets carbon-neutral operations by 2030
rows.summary: Baidu committed to achieving carbon neutrality across its operations, including its AI Cloud data centers, by 2030, paired with green power procurement and efficiency measures.

rows.headline: GDS pledges 100 percent renewable power by 2030
rows.summary: GDS states a goal to achieve operational carbon neutrality and 100 percent renewable energy usage by 2030, and to reduce its carbon footprint by increasing the proportion of renewable energy usage.

rows.headline: Google taps ENGIE for 140 MW German carbon-free portfolio
rows.summary: 140 MW is a Germany-wide ENGIE portfolio under a three-year deal from 2022, not a Hanau site figure.

rows.project: 576 MW around the clock renewables portfolio (PJM)
rows.headline: Microsoft and AES build 576 MW round the clock renewables deal
rows.summary: Microsoft signed a long term agreement with AES to source from a 576 MW portfolio of wind, solar and battery storage assets in the PJM market to deliver around the clock renewable energy to its Virginia data centers, supporting its 100/100/0 by 2030 goal.

rows.headline: Microsoft Sweden region runs on 24/7 Vattenfall clean power
rows.summary: Microsoft opened its Swedish datacenter region across Gavle, Sandviken and Staffanstorp, using Vattenfall's commercial 24/7 hourly renewable matching from wind and hydro for 100 percent renewable energy. Backup generators run on Nordic eco-labeled renewable diesel.

rows.project: Alibaba carbon neutrality and clean energy pledge
rows.headline: Alibaba commits to clean energy for its cloud
rows.summary: In its first carbon neutrality report, Alibaba pledged to reach carbon neutrality in its own operations by 2030 and to scale clean energy across Alibaba Cloud data centers, including direct renewable procurement.

rows.project: Tencent carbon neutrality and renewable pledge
rows.headline: Tencent targets carbon neutral operations by 2030
rows.summary: Tencent announced a plan to achieve carbon neutrality in its own operations and supply chain by no later than 2030, and to use green power for 100 percent of all electricity consumed by 2030.

rows.project: Finland Datacenter Region with District Heat Reuse (Espoo, Kirkkonummi)
rows.headline: Microsoft and Fortum build worlds largest datacenter heat reuse
rows.summary: Microsoft announced a Southern Finland datacenter region in Espoo and Kirkkonummi where waste heat is recycled into Fortum's district heating, described as the world's largest such scheme. It will provide about 40 percent of area district heat and cut up to 400,000 tonnes of CO2 annually. Fortum's heat pump plants have since begun operations.

rows.project: Initial 2.5 GW solar module and EPC agreement
rows.headline: Microsoft contracts 2.5 GW of Qcells solar and EPC
rows.summary: Microsoft contracted more than 2,500 MW (2.5 GW) of solar modules plus engineering, procurement and construction services from Qcells, a partnership later expanded to 12 GW in January 2024. The deal anchored US made solar supply from Qcells' Georgia operations.

rows.headline: Microsoft signs world's first fusion power purchase agreement
rows.summary: On 10 May 2023 Helion announced an agreement to provide Microsoft electricity from its first fusion power plant. Constellation will serve as the power marketer. The plant is expected to be online by 2028 and will target power generation of 50 MW or greater after a 1-year ramp up. On 16 June 2026 Helion said it continues to build Orion in Malaga, with the assembly and office building construction complete. Energized MW and COD are empty.

rows.headline: AWS commits 12.7 billion dollars to India cloud by 2030
rows.summary: AWS announced a 12.7 billion dollar investment in Indian cloud infrastructure by 2030, building on its Mumbai and Hyderabad regions. Subsequent allocations include 8.3 billion dollars in Maharashtra and 6.95 billion dollars in Telangana, supporting large-scale datacenter buildout.

rows.project: Hourly carbon free energy matching for Boydton data center
rows.headline: Microsoft signs hourly nuclear matching deal for Boydton
rows.summary: Constellation and Microsoft agreed to provide hourly carbon free energy matching for Microsoft's Boydton, Virginia data center, with the facility receiving up to 35 percent of its environmental attributes from nuclear power via Constellation's hourly matching platform. An early demonstration of 24/7 carbon free matching for data centers.

rows.project: Nuclear datacenter program (SMR and microreactor strategy)
rows.headline: Microsoft builds nuclear team to power AI with SMRs
rows.summary: Microsoft began hiring nuclear leadership, including a principal program manager for nuclear technology, to mature and implement a global small modular reactor and microreactor strategy to power its data centers. The roles signal Microsoft's intent to pursue advanced nuclear for AI compute.

rows.headline: Microsoft to invest 2.5 billion pounds in UK AI datacenters
rows.summary: Microsoft committed 2.5 billion pounds over three years to expand UK AI datacenter infrastructure in London and Cardiff, bringing more than 20,000 advanced GPUs to the UK by 2026 and more than doubling its UK datacenter footprint. It was Microsoft's largest UK investment in 40 years.

rows.project: 12 GW solar module and EPC supply alliance
rows.headline: Microsoft expands Qcells solar alliance to 12 GW
rows.summary: Microsoft expanded its strategic alliance with Qcells to procure 12,000 MW (12 GW) of US made solar modules plus engineering, procurement and construction services over eight years through 2032, building on an earlier 2.5 GW agreement. Modules are supplied from Qcells' Cartersville, Georgia factory.

rows.headline: AWS to invest 10 billion dollars in Mississippi data centers
rows.summary: AWS announced a 10 billion dollar investment in two hyperscale data center complexes in Madison County, Mississippi, the largest capital investment in state history, creating at least 1,000 jobs. Amazon later expanded its total Mississippi commitment to about 25 billion dollars.

rows.headline: Amazon takes 473 MW from Scotland Moray West wind farm
rows.summary: Amazon signed a corporate PPA with ENGIE for 473 MW of output from Ocean Winds' 882 MW Moray West offshore wind farm in Scotland, more than half the project's capacity and one of its largest single offshore wind offtakes in Europe. The wind farm reached operations in 2024 and supports Amazon's renewable energy goal.

rows.project: Cumulus data center campus at Susquehanna nuclear plant
rows.headline: AWS buys Talen nuclear-powered data center campus
rows.summary: 960 MW is power consumption and a development right, not IT under construction. AWS has a reported 480 MW cap option.

rows.project: East Anglia THREE offshore wind PPA
rows.headline: Amazon signs 159 MW UK offshore wind PPA with Iberdrola
rows.summary: Amazon signed a power purchase agreement for 159 MW from Iberdrola's 1.4 GW East Anglia THREE offshore wind farm off the coast of Suffolk, equivalent to about 700 GWh per year. Over the life of their PPAs Amazon has contracted about 54,000 GWh of renewable energy from Iberdrola.

rows.project: Japan AI and Cloud Infrastructure Expansion
rows.headline: Microsoft to invest 2.9 billion dollars in Japan AI infrastructure
rows.summary: Microsoft announced a 2.9 billion dollar investment over two years to expand hyperscale cloud and AI infrastructure in Japan, its largest investment in 46 years in the country. The plan also funds AI skilling, a Microsoft Research Asia lab, and cybersecurity work with the Japanese government.

rows.headline: Union City data center data sheet lists 202 MW
rows.summary: The EdgeConneX Atlanta data sheet lists 202 MW. There is no construction evidence, and the data sheet does not name Microsoft as tenant (tenant unverified). This row does not count.

rows.project: New Carlisle data center campus (Project Rainier)
rows.headline: AWS commits 11 billion dollars to Indiana data center campus
rows.summary: AWS announced an 11 billion dollar data center campus near New Carlisle in St. Joseph County, the largest capital investment in Indiana history. A later 15 billion dollar expansion in northern Indiana lifted Amazon's total state commitment to roughly 26 billion dollars; the campus trains AI models for Anthropic.

rows.headline: Microsoft and Brookfield frame 10.5 GW renewables buildout
rows.summary: Microsoft and Brookfield Renewable signed a five year framework agreement to develop more than 10,500 MW (10.5 GW) of new renewable energy capacity between 2026 and 2030, initially across the US and Europe, described as nearly eight times larger than the previous largest single corporate PPA. The deal supports Microsoft's 100 percent carbon free matching goal by 2030.

rows.headline: Nevada approves clean transition tariff for Google geothermal
rows.summary: Google, NV Energy, and Fervo Energy agreed on a first-of-its-kind Clean Transition Tariff under which NV Energy buys 115 MW of 24/7 enhanced geothermal power from Fervo's Corsac Station project and sells it to Google's Nevada data centers. The Public Utilities Commission of Nevada approved the tariff in May 2025. Tariff approval only. The cited link does not show a plant being built or running. The 115 MW stays on the row and does not count.

rows.project: Storey County Data Center (Tahoe Reno Industrial Center)
rows.headline: Google expands Nevada data centers near Reno
rows.summary: Google operates and continues to expand data centers at the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center in Storey County, Nevada, the anchor load behind its Fervo geothermal and NV Energy Clean Transition Tariff deals. Google has invested hundreds of millions of dollars in the Nevada campus, matched with new carbon-free geothermal supply.

rows.headline: Microsoft to invest 7.16 billion dollars in Aragon datacenters
rows.summary: Microsoft is investing about 6.69 billion euros (roughly 7.16 billion dollars) over ten years to build a data center cluster near Zaragoza in Aragon, northeastern Spain, building on a separate 2.1 billion dollar 2024 to 2025 AI and cloud commitment tied to its Spain Central region.

rows.counterparty: Nvidia / Supermicro / Dell (GPU and server supply)
rows.headline: Colossus 1: approximately 130 megawatts of compute power, brought online in 122 days
rows.summary: SpaceX's 12 June 2026 Form 424B4 says: At COLOSSUS, we brought online the first cluster of approximately 100,000 H100 processors, approximately 130 megawatts of compute power, in just 122 days. This is the only filing-backed figure for Colossus 1, and it is a floor. Energized MW is empty. The duplicate Memphis row does not count.

rows.headline: Meta signs 150 MW geothermal deal with Sage Geosystems
rows.summary: Meta agreed to buy up to 150 MW of next generation geothermal power from Sage Geosystems using its Geopressured Geothermal Systems. Phase one is targeted to be operational by 2027 at an undisclosed site east of the Rocky Mountains. Houston reflects the Sage Geosystems headquarters, not a confirmed plant location.

rows.headline: AWS plans 8 billion pounds for UK datacenters
rows.summary: AWS announced plans to invest 8 billion pounds over five years (2024 to 2028) to build and operate UK data centers, estimated to add 14 billion pounds to UK GDP and support more than 14,000 jobs annually.

rows.project: Crane Clean Energy Center (Three Mile Island Unit 1 restart)
rows.headline: Microsoft revives Three Mile Island with 20 year nuclear PPA
rows.summary: Microsoft signed a 20 year power purchase agreement with Constellation Energy to restart Three Mile Island Unit 1, renamed the Crane Clean Energy Center, a retired 835 MW reactor. Constellation has since accelerated the targeted restart to 2027 and secured a $1 billion DOE loan to support the project. Primary source announces the restart; no primary evidence of site work yet.

rows.project: Kairos Power SMR Fleet (Master Plant Development Agreement)
rows.headline: Google signs first corporate deal for SMR fleet
rows.summary: Google and Kairos Power signed a Master Plant Development Agreement to deploy a fleet of advanced fluoride-salt-cooled reactors totaling 500 MW by 2035, with the first plant targeted online by 2030. It is the first corporate agreement for multiple deployments of a single advanced reactor design in the US, with energy sold to Google under long-term PPAs.

rows.headline: Amazon leads 500 million dollar X-energy SMR raise
rows.summary: Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund anchored an approximately 500 million dollar Series C-1 financing round for SMR developer X-energy, alongside Citadel's Ken Griffin, Ares Management affiliates, NGP and the University of Michigan. The investment supports development of X-energy's Xe-100 high-temperature gas reactor toward a goal of 5 GW online by 2039.

rows.headline: Amazon backs Energy Northwest SMR project in Washington
rows.summary: Amazon agreed to support an initial four-unit, 320 MW X-energy Xe-100 SMR project with Energy Northwest near the Columbia Generating Station, with an option to expand to 12 units (about 960 MW). Now named the Cascade Advanced Energy Facility, first power is targeted for the early 2030s.

rows.headline: Amazon and Dominion explore SMR at North Anna
rows.summary: Amazon and Dominion Energy Virginia signed a memorandum of understanding to explore deploying a small modular reactor near the North Anna nuclear station, aiming to add at least 300 MW of new capacity to the Virginia grid. The MOU does not commit to a specific reactor design or guarantee construction.

rows.project: Global renewable energy portfolio (600+ wind and solar projects)
rows.headline: Amazon ranked world's largest corporate renewables buyer
rows.summary: Amazon was named the world's largest corporate buyer of renewable energy for a fifth consecutive year based on BloombergNEF data, backing more than 600 wind and solar projects globally. The company reports the portfolio can generate energy equivalent to powering millions of US homes when fully operational.

rows.headline: Meta seeks up to 4 GW of new nuclear for AI
rows.summary: Meta issued a request for proposals seeking 1 to 4 GW of new nuclear generation, open to both large reactors and SMRs, with delivery targeted for the early 2030s. The RFP drew more than 50 qualified submissions across 20 states, with initial proposals due February 2025. The 4 GW figure is the top of the range, not a firm contracted amount.

rows.headline: Meta expands Hyperion to a 5 GW compute target
rows.summary: Meta expanded its Richland Parish Hyperion campus to a 5,000 MW compute target. The figure is a compute target, not generation and not COD. Entergy gas and related generation packages are tracked on separate rows and are not added here. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.headline: Google backs 20 billion dollar co-located energy parks
rows.summary: Google, Intersect Power, and TPG Rise Climate announced a partnership to build industrial parks with gigawatts of data center capacity co-located with new clean power, with Intersect targeting $20 billion in renewable infrastructure investment by the end of the decade. Google acts as offtaker and anchor tenant, with the first co-located project expected operational by 2026.

rows.headline: OpenAI and partners launch $500B Stargate AI buildout
rows.summary: OpenAI, SoftBank, Oracle, and MGX announced the Stargate Project at the White House on January 21, 2025, a plan to invest $500 billion over four years building AI infrastructure in the U.S., targeting 10 GW (10,000 MW) with $100 billion deployed immediately. SoftBank holds financial responsibility and OpenAI operational responsibility.

rows.headline: Amazon adds 3 billion dollar Warren County data center campus
rows.summary: Amazon announced at least 3 billion dollars for a next-generation data center campus in Warren County (Vicksburg), Mississippi, the largest private investment in the county's history. It followed the earlier 10 billion dollar Madison County project and lifted Amazon's total Mississippi commitment toward 25 billion dollars.

rows.headline: Crusoe expands flagship Abilene Stargate campus to 1.2 GW
rows.summary: Crusoe Energy, on the Lancium Clean Campus near Abilene, is developing Stargate's flagship data center to 1.2 GW (1,200 MW) across eight buildings, running on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure for OpenAI. The first two buildings went live in 2025 with full buildout targeted for mid-2026. A planned 600 MW expansion beyond 1.2 GW was later scrapped.

rows.counterparty: Crusoe Energy, Engine No. 1, GE Vernova
rows.headline: Crusoe secures 4.5 GW natural gas to power Abilene AI campus
rows.summary: Crusoe partnered with investment firm Engine No. 1 to secure up to 4.5 GW (4,500 MW) of behind-the-meter natural gas generation, with GE Vernova supplying aeroderivative gas turbines including a 29-unit LM2500XPRESS deal, to power the Abilene Stargate campus. The 4,500 MW figure is reported by trade press. It is not the TCEQ 177263 permitted plant (360.5 MW at the Crusoe Longhorn site). The two rows are never added.

rows.counterparty: Engine No. 1 (GE Vernova and Chevron turbines)
rows.project: Crusoe behind-the-meter natural gas for AI
rows.headline: Crusoe secures 4.5 gigawatts of natural gas for AI
rows.summary: Crusoe partnered with investment firm Engine No. 1 to secure about 4.5 GW of natural gas power for AI data centers using GE Vernova turbines, generating power directly for compute and bypassing traditional grids. Separately Crusoe ordered 29 GE Vernova turbines providing nearly 1 GW.

rows.counterparty: Tesla (Megapack) / Memphis Light Gas and Water (MLGW)
rows.project: Colossus 1 onsite power: gas turbines, Megapack and MLGW substation
rows.headline: Colossus 1 powered by 35 gas turbines (422 MW), 168 Tesla Megapacks and a 150 MW MLGW substation
rows.summary: To power Colossus 1 ahead of full grid interconnection, xAI deployed 35 onsite natural gas turbines rated at a combined 422 MW plus 168 Tesla Megapack battery units for buffering. xAI also built a 150 MW MLGW substation in about 97 days. The gas turbines drew scrutiny and a lawsuit from environmental groups over Clean Air Act permitting.

rows.headline: Google signs Taiwan first corporate geothermal PPA
rows.summary: Google signed Taiwan's first corporate geothermal power purchase agreement with Baseload Capital for 10 MW of always-on power, plus a direct equity investment, to supply its Taiwan data centers and offices. The capacity is expected online around 2029 and roughly doubles Taiwan's installed geothermal base.

rows.counterparty: Crusoe Energy, GE Vernova, Solar Turbines
rows.headline: TCEQ permit lists 360.5 MW of on-site turbines at the Crusoe Longhorn site
rows.summary: TCEQ Electric Generating Unit Standard Permit technical review for registration 177263 lists five 38 MW Titan 350 turbines and five 34.1 MW GE LM2500 turbines, 360.5 MW, to generate power for onsite use only at the Crusoe Longhorn Data Center. The registration was issued 22 January 2025. An issued permit is not construction evidence, so this row does not count. This 360.5 MW permit is the older Abilene on-site figure for the Crusoe Longhorn site. It is the same site as the 900 MW announced on-site row (microsoft-crusoe-abilene-2-btm-900). Those rows are never added. The 4,500 MW Abilene figure reported by trade press is not this plant. Energized MW and COD are empty.
rows.sourceName: TCEQ EGU standard permit technical review 177263

rows.headline: Crusoe expands Abilene Stargate campus to 1.2 gigawatts
rows.summary: Crusoe is developing the Lancium Clean Campus in Abilene, Texas to 1.2 GW across eight buildings, the flagship site of OpenAI's Stargate. Crusoe secured 11.6 billion dollars in 2025 to expand from two to eight buildings; Oracle leases the site for OpenAI, with the first buildings live.

rows.headline: Google funds three 600 MW nuclear development sites
rows.summary: Google signed a strategic agreement to provide early-stage development capital to Elementl Power for three advanced nuclear project sites in the US, each at least 600 MW, for a combined 1.8 GW. The technology-agnostic, site-first approach positions the projects for future reactor selection, with Google holding an option to buy the power once operational. Site locations were not disclosed.

rows.headline: AWS and HUMAIN back 5 billion dollar Saudi AI Zone
rows.summary: AWS and Saudi PIF backed HUMAIN announced a more than 5 billion dollar partnership to build a dedicated AI Zone in Saudi Arabia for training and deploying AI, including Arabic large language models. A November 2025 expansion added plans to deploy up to 150,000 AI accelerators using NVIDIA GB300 and AWS Trainium chips.

rows.headline: OpenAI and G42 launch 1 GW Stargate UAE cluster
rows.summary: The 1 GW is the cluster target. The first 200 MW under construction is a separate row.

rows.headline: G42 is building the first 200 MW of the Stargate UAE cluster
rows.summary: G42's 16 October 2025 release says it is building the first 200MW of the 1GW Stargate UAE cluster. This row is that 200 MW. The 1 GW stays on the parent as the cluster target.

rows.headline: Google deepens fusion bet with TAE Technologies
rows.summary: Google participated in TAE Technologies' funding round of more than $150 million alongside Chevron and NEA, building on its investment in the California fusion company since 2015. Google has collaborated with TAE on machine learning for fusion since 2015, supporting TAE's roadmap toward its first prototype power plant, Da Vinci, in the early 2030s.

rows.headline: Meta signs 20 year nuclear deal for Clinton plant
rows.summary: Meta signed a 20-year PPA for 1,121 MW from Constellation's Clinton Clean Energy Center in Illinois, beginning June 2027. The deal supports relicensing of the plant and adds 30 MW via uprates after the state ZEC program expires in mid-2027.

rows.project: Pennsylvania data center expansion (Falls and Salem townships)
rows.headline: Amazon to invest 20 billion dollars in Pennsylvania data centers
rows.summary: Amazon announced at least 20 billion dollars in Pennsylvania data center investment, the largest capital investment in state history, with initial campuses in Falls Township (Bucks County) and Salem Township (Luzerne County). The Salem Township site sits adjacent to the Susquehanna nuclear plant and the project is expected to create at least 1,250 permanent jobs.

rows.headline: Talen and Amazon sign 18 billion dollar nuclear PPA
rows.summary: Talen Energy and Amazon signed a 17-year, roughly 18 billion dollar power purchase agreement to supply up to 1,920 MW of carbon-free nuclear power from the Susquehanna plant, ramping to 840 to 1,200 MW by 2029 and 1,680 to 1,920 MW by 2032. The grid-connected structure replaced an earlier 300 MW co-location arrangement, and the parties agreed to explore SMRs and uprates.

rows.headline: Meta and XGS Energy partner on 150 MW geothermal in New Mexico
rows.summary: Meta and XGS Energy announced a two-phase 150 MW advanced geothermal project on the PNM grid in New Mexico, using XGS technology that requires zero operating water. Both phases are projected operational by 2030.

rows.headline: Google buys 200 MW from Commonwealth fusion plant
rows.summary: Google signed an offtake agreement for 200 MW from Commonwealth Fusion Systems' first ARC power plant in Chesterfield County, Virginia, which CFS expects to deliver about 400 MW to the grid in the early 2030s. Google, an investor in CFS since 2021, called it the largest direct corporate offtake agreement for fusion energy and increased its equity stake.

rows.counterparty: Memphis Light Gas and Water (MLGW) / Tennessee Valley Authority
rows.headline: Colossus 1 Memphis row duplicates the 130 MW filing figure
rows.summary: This row duplicates Colossus 1. The SpaceX 424B4 figure is approximately 130 megawatts of compute power. This row does not count.

rows.project: Stateline Power JV: 900 MW natural gas supply to Colossus 2
rows.headline: Solaris-xAI joint venture to supply 900 MW of onsite gas power to Colossus
rows.summary: Solaris's 8-K describes a 900 MW on-site supply for the same Southaven plant at 2875 Stanton Road. That 900 MW is a subset of the MDEQ permit for the plant and is not a second counted row.

rows.headline: CoreWeave to control 1.3 gigawatts via Core Scientific deal
rows.summary: On July 7, 2025 CoreWeave agreed to acquire Core Scientific in an all-stock deal, gaining about 1.3 GW of gross power across a national data center footprint plus an incremental 1 GW or more available for expansion. The deal later collapsed when Core Scientific shareholders rejected it.

rows.headline: CoreWeave plans up to 6 billion dollars for a Lancaster data center
rows.summary: CoreWeave announced its intent to commit up to 6 billion dollars to a data center in Lancaster, Pennsylvania. The initial site is 100 MW, with potential to expand to 300 MW.

rows.headline: Meta offtakes 600 MW Enbridge solar near San Antonio
rows.summary: Enbridge announced the $900 million, 600 MW Clear Fork Solar Project in Wilson County, Texas, with Meta contracting 100 percent of the output for its regional data centers. The project is targeted for service in summer 2027.

rows.headline: OpenAI and Oracle add 4.5 GW of Stargate capacity
rows.summary: OpenAI and Oracle agreed to develop up to 4.5 GW (4,500 MW) of additional Stargate data center capacity in the U.S., a partnership exceeding $300 billion over five years. Combined with Abilene, it brings OpenAI to over 5 GW of capacity under development.

rows.headline: Palisades restart is in progress
rows.summary: Holtec's Palisades plant in Covert Township, Michigan, about 805 MW nameplate, is a restart in progress. It is not shown as operating, and energized MW is empty. The restart is backed by a DOE loan guarantee. This row is offtake from an existing plant and is not in the firm offtake total.

rows.headline: TVA buys nuclear from Kairos Hermes 2 for Google
rows.summary: Google, Kairos Power, and TVA announced a collaboration in which TVA signed a PPA to buy up to 50 MW from Kairos Power's Hermes 2 plant in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, delivering 24/7 energy to the grid serving Google data centers in Tennessee and Alabama. It is the first deployment under Google's 500 MW Kairos deal and the first US utility PPA for a Gen IV reactor, with operations targeted for 2030. NRC construction permit, pending docket confirmation. It becomes construction only on evidence of work at Hermes 2 itself.

rows.project: Lake Mariner AI hosting (CB-3/4 and CB-5)
rows.headline: TeraWulf will provide 378 MW of critical IT at Lake Mariner
rows.summary: TeraWulf's Q1 2026 10-Q says "we will provide 378 MW of critical IT load at the Lake Mariner Data Campus" and "construction having commenced in 2025".

rows.project: Entergy combined-cycle gas plants for Hyperion (initial three)
rows.headline: LPSC certified three Entergy gas plants for Meta, not yet under construction
rows.summary: LPSC certified. Entergy Louisiana application: https://s201.q4cdn.com/714390239/files/doc_downloads/2024/10/E-LA-application.pdf. Entergy news: https://www.entergy.com/news/entergy-louisiana-receives-lpsc-approval-for-major-infrastructure-investments-to-support-metas-data-center-and-improve-reliability. EIA 860M August 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/august_generator2026.xlsx) lists Franklin Farms 1560.6 MW as status L and Waterford 5 820 MW as status T, both not under construction. EIA nameplate is 2,380.6 MW. It counts when 860M shows U or V. Do not add the Richland Parish 1 to 4 or Waterford 6 plants to anything.

rows.counterparty: Tesla (AI4 chip and Digital Optimus agent) / Nvidia (servers)
rows.headline: Musk announces Macrohard, an all-AI software company to rival Microsoft
rows.summary: Elon Musk announced Macrohard, a tongue-in-cheek named but real all-AI software venture under xAI meant to simulate software companies like Microsoft entirely with AI. xAI filed a Macrohard trademark on August 1, 2025. In March 2026 Musk unveiled a joint Tesla-xAI implementation pairing Grok as a navigator with a Tesla screen-watching agent, running on Tesla's AI4 chip plus xAI's Nvidia servers. A Southaven building tied to the Colossus 2 expansion is named MACROHARDRR.

rows.headline: CoreWeave's Ellendale contract is 400 MW, and 250 MW is counted
rows.summary: 400 MW contracted across three leases. 250 MW counted. The last 150 MW is not counted: Applied Digital's FY2026 10-K says "under construction" in Item 1 (printed p.6) but "currently in the design phase" in Note 17 (printed p.119). It returns to the count only when a primary shows work at that hall. On 30 Mar 2026 the ELN-02 lease was amended to suspend two of four halls, and a new lease for those halls was signed with CoreWeave Compute Acquisition Co. VIII, LLC. The ELN-03 lease was assigned to the same subsidiary. The 400 MW contract total is unchanged. ELN-02 is the 100 MW hall. ELN-03 is the second 150 MW hall. Building 4 is the last 150 MW hall. Operational per company: Item 1 says the first approximately 100 MW became operational in October 2025 and that the second 150 MW is partially operational. Note 17 says the 100 MW hall became operational in November 2025. CLAIM, per the company's earnings release: "Achieved Ready for Service for Phase 1 of Building 2 (75 MW) at Polaris Forge 1 on schedule, bringing total live capacity at the campus to 175 MW." The release says that delivery was on June 30, 2026. The release's Building 2 is the 10-K's ELN-03. Note 17 calls the 100 MW ELN-02 hall Building 2 and calls the 150 MW ELN-03 hall Building 3. These statements are company CLAIM and are not measured energized load. Energized MW is empty.

rows.headline: xAI builds first gigawatt-scale AI data center near Memphis
rows.summary: This 1,100 MW figure is a turbine and grid-request range, not IT. It duplicates the Colossus II IT row, which counts the SpaceX filing's approximately 210 MW plus 220 MW of compute. This row does not count.

rows.headline: Microsoft opens 3.3 billion dollar Fairwater AI campus in Wisconsin
rows.summary: Microsoft's 3.3 billion dollar Fairwater AI datacenter in Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin, announced in September 2025 on a 315 acre site once intended for Foxconn, came online ahead of schedule in early 2026 housing hundreds of thousands of Nvidia GB200 GPUs. Microsoft describes it as the world's most powerful AI datacenter.

rows.headline: Microsoft adds 4 billion dollar second Wisconsin AI datacenter
rows.summary: Microsoft committed a further 4 billion dollars to build a second AI datacenter of similar scale adjacent to Fairwater in Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin, lifting total Wisconsin investment to more than 7 billion dollars. The expansion is expected to be completed by 2028.

rows.headline: Oracle-led Stargate site planned in Shackelford County
rows.summary: Among five new Stargate sites announced in September 2025, Shackelford County, Texas is an Oracle-developed campus. The three Oracle sites plus an Abilene expansion together targeted over 5.5 GW, but per-site capacity was not individually disclosed.

rows.project: Stargate Dona Ana County, New Mexico
rows.headline: Oracle-led Stargate campus planned in southern New Mexico
rows.summary: Dona Ana County, New Mexico is one of three new Oracle-developed Stargate campuses announced in September 2025. The three Oracle sites plus an Abilene expansion combine for over 5.5 GW, but per-site capacity was not individually disclosed.

rows.headline: Stargate Milam County site, no primary MW yet
rows.summary: The TDLR record TABS2026017746 (https://www.tdlr.texas.gov/TABS/Search/Project/TABS2026017746) shows new construction at the site, but no primary source yet gives Milam-specific MW. Pending review Monday.

rows.headline: SoftBank breaks ground on Lordstown Stargate site
rows.summary: SoftBank broke ground on an advanced data center design in Lordstown, Ohio, on track to be operational in 2026, doubling as a SoftBank-Foxconn manufacturing hub for AI servers. Site capacity was not individually disclosed; Lordstown and Milam County together can scale to 1.5 GW.

rows.headline: Vistra signs 20-year nuclear PPA for Comanche Peak
rows.summary: On September 29, 2025 Vistra announced a 20-year power purchase agreement, with options for up to 20 more years, to supply 1,200 MW of carbon-free power from its Comanche Peak nuclear plant in Texas to an unnamed investment-grade customer. Deliveries begin in Q4 2027 and ramp to full volume by 2032.

rows.project: Bloom and Brookfield fuel cell partnership
rows.headline: Brookfield and Bloom announce a fuel cell partnership
rows.summary: Bloom Energy's 13 October 2025 release says Brookfield will invest up to $5 billion to deploy Bloom fuel cells for AI factories. The release does not state a megawatt figure for the partnership (EMPTY PRIMARY for the figure). The 1,000 MW stored on this row is not in that release and does not count. San Jose reflects the Bloom Energy headquarters, not a single project site.

rows.headline: Google commits 15 billion dollars to India AI hub
rows.summary: Google, AdaniConneX, and Airtel announced a gigawatt-scale AI hub in Visakhapatnam. The release says gigawatt-scale and does not state a megawatt figure, so capacity is empty. This row does not count.

rows.headline: Amazon details 12-unit Cascade SMR plan in Washington
rows.summary: In an October 2025 update, Amazon and Energy Northwest detailed plans to ultimately deploy 12 Xe-100 SMRs (about 960 MW) at the Cascade Advanced Energy Facility near Richland, starting with the first four units. A joint venture of Aecon, Kiewit Nuclear Solutions and Black and Veatch was selected for the first phase, with construction targeted by 2030.

rows.headline: Vantage is building the Port Washington campus for Oracle
rows.summary: Vantage's 27 April 2026 release says the Port Washington campus is being built by Vantage for Oracle. The cited release shows no MW figure (EMPTY PRIMARY for the figure). The campus page states 902 MW of critical IT load and is undated. The 902 MW stays on the row and does not count.

rows.headline: Anthropic expands Google TPU deal to one gigawatt by 2026
rows.summary: In October 2025 Anthropic announced a major expansion of its use of Google Cloud TPUs, with well over a gigawatt of capacity coming online in 2026 and access to up to one million TPU chips. The broader Google Cloud deal is valued in the tens of billions of dollars.

rows.headline: Meta and ENGIE sign 600 MW Texas solar PPA
rows.summary: Meta signed a PPA for 100 percent of the output of ENGIE's 600 MW Swenson Ranch Solar project in Stonewall County, Texas, the largest asset in ENGIE's US portfolio. The deal expanded the Meta-ENGIE partnership past 1.3 GW across four Texas solar projects. Operations begin in 2027.

rows.project: Duane Arnold Energy Center nuclear restart
rows.headline: Google backs restart of Iowa Duane Arnold nuclear plant
rows.summary: Google signed a 25-year power purchase agreement with NextEra Energy to restart the 615 MW Duane Arnold Energy Center in Palo, Iowa, shuttered since 2020, to power its Iowa data centers. The restart targets the first quarter of 2029, with NextEra moving to full ownership.

rows.headline: Building 168 MW of critical IT at Abernathy
rows.summary: TeraWulf's Q1 2026 10-Q says the Abernathy HPC Campus is designed for 168 MW of critical IT load and that construction is proceeding in phases. The same filing says the company holds a 50.1% equity interest in the joint venture.

rows.counterparty: Oracle, Related Digital, Blackstone, Walbridge, and DTE
rows.project: Stargate The Barn, Saline Township, Michigan
rows.headline: Stargate Saline campus under construction, more than 1 GW
rows.summary: OpenAI describes the Stargate campus in Saline Township as more than 1 GW. Oracle says all campus buildings are now actively under construction. Energized MW and COD are empty.

rows.headline: Holtec wins DOE award for twin SMR-300 at Palisades
rows.summary: Holtec received a DOE Tier 1 First Mover award of 400 million dollars to deploy its dual-unit SMR-300 plant (680 MWe total, 340 MWe per unit) named PIONEER 1&2 at the Palisades Energy site in Michigan, targeting the early 2030s. Holtec filed a Limited Work Authorization application with the NRC in December 2025.

rows.headline: Microsoft and G42 add 200 MW of UAE datacenter capacity
rows.summary: Possible duplicate of stargate-uae-phase1-200, never counted alongside it.

rows.project: Germany Data Center and AI Expansion (Dietzenbach, Hanau)
rows.headline: Google to invest 5.5 billion euros in German AI infrastructure
rows.summary: Google announced a 5.5 billion euro investment in Germany through 2029, including a new data center in Dietzenbach, continued buildout at the Hanau campus, and expanded offices, alongside ongoing 24/7 carbon-free energy commitments with ENGIE.

rows.project: Anthropic custom AI data centers (Texas and New York)
rows.headline: Anthropic commits 50 billion dollars to US AI data centers
rows.summary: Anthropic announced a 50 billion dollar plan to build custom US data centers with partner Fluidstack, starting in Texas and New York, with first sites going live in 2026. The build is projected to create about 800 permanent and 2,400 construction jobs.

rows.headline: Microsoft links Atlanta and Wisconsin into AI superfactory
rows.summary: Microsoft launched its second Fairwater AI datacenter outside Atlanta, Georgia, a two story facility with hundreds of thousands of Nvidia GB200 and GB300 GPUs, directly networked to the Wisconsin site over a dedicated AI WAN to operate as a distributed AI superfactory. The Atlanta facility began operating in October 2025.

rows.headline: Cipher is building 168 MW of critical IT at Barber Lake
rows.summary: Cipher's Q2 2026 10-Q says it is in the process of building the Barber Lake Facility for Fluidstack. The lease 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1819989/000095010325012168/dp234624_8k.htm) says the facility is expected to provide 168 megawatts (MW) of critical IT load. A later Cipher 8-K says individual data halls are now expected to be delivered between the fourth quarter of 2026 and the first quarter of 2027. Rent will commence for each data hall as it is delivered, with the first rent commencement expected to occur during the fourth quarter of 2026. Energized MW and COD are empty.

rows.project: River Bend AI data center lease
rows.headline: Hut 8 lists 245 MW of critical IT at River Bend
rows.summary: Hut 8's Q2 2026 10-Q says the River Bend lease is 245 megawatts of critical IT capacity. Hut 8 is the developer. The 330 MW figure is the site, not this IT row.

rows.headline: Alphabet buys clean energy developer Intersect Power
rows.summary: Alphabet announced a definitive agreement to acquire clean energy and data center infrastructure developer Intersect Power for about $4.75 billion in cash plus assumed debt, deepening its strategy of pairing data center load with co-located clean generation. The deal, expected to close in the first half of 2026, brings Intersect's renewables and storage development portfolio in-house.

rows.headline: Colossus II: about 210 MW plus 220 MW of compute power, brought online
rows.summary: SpaceX's 12 June 2026 Form 424B4 says the first cluster has approximately 210 megawatts of compute power and the second cluster has 220 megawatts of compute power, and that both were brought online. The filing names Tulane Road in Memphis, Tennessee and Stateline Road in Southaven, Mississippi, and does not say which cluster is where. The pin is not an exact site. Energized MW is empty. The 1,100 MW Southaven row is a duplicate of this IT figure and is not counted.

rows.project: Vistra Perry, Davis-Besse, Beaver Valley nuclear PPAs
rows.headline: Meta and Vistra sign 20 year deal for 2,609 MW nuclear
rows.summary: As part of Meta's January 2026 nuclear announcement, Vistra signed 20-year PPAs to supply 2,609 MW of nuclear power in PJM, including 2,176 MW from the operating Perry and Davis-Besse plants plus uprates across Perry, Davis-Besse, and Beaver Valley, phasing in through 2034. Irving reflects Vistra headquarters; the plants are in Ohio and Pennsylvania.

rows.headline: Meta backs TerraPower Natrium reactors up to 2.8 GW
rows.summary: Meta's agreement funds development of up to eight 345 MW Natrium sodium fast reactors providing up to 2.8 GW of baseload power, with built-in storage able to boost output toward 4 GW. Two initial units of about 690 MW are targeted for delivery as early as 2032, with the remaining units targeted by 2035.

rows.project: Oklo Pike County Ohio power campus
rows.headline: Meta and Oklo plan 1.2 GW nuclear campus in Ohio
rows.summary: Meta agreed with Oklo to help develop a 1.2 GW nuclear power campus in Pike County, Ohio, using Aurora Powerhouse reactors to support Meta data centers in the region. Pre-construction and site characterization begin in 2026, with the first phase targeted as early as 2030 and full capacity by 2034.

rows.headline: Google signs 1.17 GW renewable deal with Clearway
rows.summary: Google signed PPAs totaling about 1.17 GW of solar and wind capacity with Clearway Energy Group across Missouri, Texas, and West Virginia, representing roughly $2.4 billion in clean energy investment. The projects span the SPP, ERCOT, and PJM markets under agreements of up to 20 years, with initial sites coming online in 2027 and 2028.

rows.headline: Fervo says the first 33 MW block at Cape Station is in commercial operation (company claim)
rows.summary: CLAIM. Per Fervo's 1 Oct 2026 release (8-K Exhibit 99.1), Cape Station declared commercial operation on Sep 30, 2026, one day before its contractual COD. The release says the first of three 33 MW GeoBlocks produced 33 MW net and is generating revenue under its PPA. The remaining two Phase I blocks are expected to reach contractual COD by Jan 1, 2027. The release names no buyer. This is a company claim, not measured energized load.

rows.counterparty: Southaven / DeSoto County, Mississippi (former Duke Energy plant site)
rows.project: Colossus 2 Southaven gas turbine fleet and MACROHARDRR building
rows.headline: MDEQ permit for about 1.2 GW at 2875 Stanton Road
rows.summary: MDEQ Air Construction PSD permit 0680-00119, issued 11 March 2026 to MZX Tech LLC at 2875 Stanton Road, Southaven, is the source for about 1.2 GW. An issued permit is not evidence of construction, and the 1,200 MW figure has not been verified against the permit text, so this row does not count. The Solaris 900 MW 8-K is a subset of the same plant and is not a second row. MDEQ Agreed Order 7739 26 is not added. Lawsuits allege operation without required permits. Those are allegations only. Energized MW is empty.

rows.project: SoftBank Portsmouth (Piketon) Ohio AI campus and gas plants
rows.headline: SoftBank plans 10 GW Ohio AI campus on gas power
rows.summary: SoftBank plans a roughly 10 GW AI data center on a former DOE uranium enrichment site near Piketon, Ohio, backed by up to 10 GW of new power generation including about 9.2 GW of natural gas, with a reported $33 billion power investment. Sources describe it as part of a U.S.-Japan investment program and not formally part of Stargate. Capacity and siting remain early.

rows.project: Entergy seven additional gas plants for Hyperion
rows.headline: Meta triples gas order with seven more Entergy plants
rows.summary: Meta and Entergy announced an agreement for seven additional gas plants totaling about 5.2 GW on top of the initial three, bringing the Hyperion campus to 10 plants and roughly 7.5 GW. Meta also committed to fund up to 2.5 GW of renewables and storage plus 240 miles of transmission. The LPSC adopted a fast-track review schedule in April 2026; approval pending.

rows.project: Meridian Arc Sullivan County AI campus
rows.headline: Meridian Arc finances 430 MW critical IT campus in Indiana
rows.summary: Meridian Arc HoldCo, a Next Frontier and Fluidstack joint venture, priced senior secured notes to finance two turnkey halls totaling 430 MW of critical IT load (245 MW plus 185 MW) in Sullivan County, Indiana. Latham advised the offering; Fitch rated the notes BB. The figure is contracted IT, not generation. Google lease guarantees are credit support, not electrons. Behind-the-meter versus grid megawatt-hour mix is not disclosed in the primary.

rows.headline: Chevron signs a 20-year PPA for about 2.67 GW at Project Kilby
rows.summary: On 22 June 2026 Chevron said Energy Forge One signed a 20-year power purchase agreement with Microsoft for Project Kilby, a co-located gas plant expected to deliver approximately 2.67 gigawatts. The project page describes generation behind the meter in Reeves County, Texas. ERCOT GIS for August 2026 lists Kilby with no interconnection agreement. The 2,377 MW gas figure is a studied maximum net export, not plant size. The map pin is the U.S. Census internal point for Reeves County (31.308366 N, 103.712706 W), a county reference point, not a surveyed plant site. Energized MW and COD are empty. This row is announced on-site generation and is not in the firm on-site total.

rows.headline: Anthropic and Amazon expand to up to 5 gigawatts of compute
rows.summary: Anthropic and Amazon expanded their collaboration for up to 5 GW of new AWS compute to train and serve Claude, including significant Trainium2 and Trainium3 capacity through 2026. Amazon is investing 5 billion dollars now plus up to 20 billion more, on top of 8 billion previously invested.

rows.headline: Meta expands RWE partnership with 298 MW Texas solar
rows.summary: Meta signed a long-term PPA for the 298 MW Rabbit's Foot Solar project in Bowie County, northeast Texas, the fourth PPA between Meta and RWE. Construction began in 2026 with commissioning expected by the end of 2027.

rows.headline: Meta breaks ground on 1 GW Sturgeon County data center
rows.summary: Meta broke ground on its first Canadian data center, a 1,000 MW DC campus in Sturgeon County, Alberta. The figure is DC capacity only. Pembina and Greenlight took FID on a 932 MW behind-the-meter gas plant to serve the site; that generation is not added on this row. An 1,864 MW expandable generation case is a scenario, not a row. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.headline: TeraWulf leases Anthropic 401 MW critical IT at Justified
rows.summary: TeraWulf signed a 20-year lease with Anthropic for about 401 MW of critical IT load at the Justified Data campus in Hawesville, Kentucky. The Kentucky PSC later approved a 482 MW RESA for the campus; that utility path is not additive to the 401 MW IT figure. This row is Anthropic at Justified, not Fluidstack. The existing Abernathy 168 MW Fluidstack pin is unchanged. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.headline: Hut 8 signs second 352 MW IT lease at Beacon Point
rows.summary: Hut 8 commercialized Beacon Point Phase 2 in Nueces County, Texas with a second 352 MW IT lease. The primary does not name the buyer; this row does not invent Anthropic, Lambda, or NVIDIA. Phase 1 is not already in Atlas, so only this +352 IT increment is appended. Campus-level 704 MW IT is not the same as the 1,000 MW AEP Texas utility interconnection. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.headline: OpenAI takes 8 IT-GW at PORTS-Pike, 4.25 firm plus 3.75 option
rows.summary: NVIDIA guaranteed SB Energy's PORTS-Pike campus in Pike County, Ohio to host NVIDIA AI compute, with OpenAI as the customer for 8,000 IT MW labeled 4,250 MW firm plus 3,750 MW option under a 20-year lease. This row is buyer IT only. Planned SB Energy generation of at least 10 GW is not added here; the existing SoftBank Piketon generation pin stays separate. Separate from Stargate Abilene and from Camellia. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.headline: Georgia PSC approves OpenAI 3,200 MW contracted demand
rows.summary: The Georgia Public Service Commission approved Georgia Power's contract to serve OpenAI's Camellia project in Effingham County at 3,200 MW of contracted demand, not COD. Flexible demand response of up to 1,000 MW sits inside the 3,200 MW, not as an extra 1,000 MW. Delivery is 2028-2032. Separate from Stargate Abilene and from PORTS-Pike. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.headline: Google signs 396 MW firm geothermal PPA at Cape Station
rows.summary: Fervo Energy and Google signed a 396 MW firm enhanced geothermal PPA at Cape Station in Beaver County, Utah, announced 1 September 2026. The figure is offtake, not plant ownership. An option of about 600 MW is not firm and is not added here. The earlier Cape Station pin of about 100 MW stays on its own row. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.headline: Google takes a derived 507 MW share of Loviisa nuclear
rows.summary: Fortum and Google signed a 22-year life-extension PPA for up to 50 percent of the Loviisa nuclear plant. Capacity is a derived offtake share: two units at about 507 MWe each, so 50 percent is 507 MW. The row is never the 1,014 MWe plant total. Planned plant uprates of about 38 MW and 10 MW are not added to Google. The PPA is high confidence; the 507 MW absolute is medium because it is derived. Hamina, Kajaani, Muhos, and Vaala site megawatts from the EUR 13 billion package are not invented here. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.headline: Google contracts 94 MW battery storage in Kajaani
rows.summary: Google contracted a 94 MW battery system near its Kajaani site, with Fortum signed to optimize the storage. The figure is storage, not generation, and is kept off generation heroes. Expected operation is late 2027. This row does not invent data-center megawatts for Hamina, Kajaani, Muhos, or Vaala. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.headline: Google Finland wind portfolio stands at 629 MW
rows.summary: Google said two onshore wind projects with Valorem and Suomen Hyotytuuli bring the total new-to-the-grid onshore wind it has contracted in Finland to 629 MW. No prior Finland wind row existed, so this is one portfolio pin at 629, not a new +629 incremental deal. Delta is empty. This is offtake, not a week total with Loviisa or Kajaani storage. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.headline: Aligned breaks ground on 2 GW Project Phoenix campus
rows.summary: Aligned Data Centers broke ground on Project Phoenix, a 2,000 MW landlord campus in Shippingport, Pennsylvania. The end tenant is unnamed. The figure is landlord campus DC capacity only, not interconnection and not COD. Adjacent onsite generation at the former Shippingport power site is not added on this row. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.project: Texas Critical Data Center (TCDC) Phase 1 PPA
rows.headline: New Era contracts 207 MW firm offtake for TCDC Phase 1
rows.summary: TCDC PowerCo LLC, a subsidiary of New Era Energy & Digital, signed a 20-year power purchase agreement with Luminant ET Services Company LLC, an affiliate of Vistra, on 18 September 2026. The company announced the deal on 21 September 2026. Luminant will supply a Contract Quantity of 200 MW minimum and 207 MW maximum for Phase 1 of the Texas Critical Data Center (TCDC) on property near Vistra's Odessa, Texas gas plant. This row pins the 207 MW maximum. The Odessa plant nameplate of about 1,180 MW is not the contracted quantity and is not campus load. No hyperscaler tenant is named, and tenant IT megawatts are not on this row. Conditions precedent, including the Phase 1 substation purchase agreement, run through 31 December 2027. Delivery is targeted for the third quarter of 2027. Power may also be sourced from other available supply or the ERCOT grid. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.headline: Oracle matches 433 MW from existing Panther Creek wind
rows.summary: RWE signed a 433 MW virtual power purchase agreement with Oracle on 17 September 2026 for output from the existing Panther Creek I, II, and III wind farms in Sterling, Howard, and Glasscock counties, West Texas. This is carbon matching for Oracle data center operations on the Texas grid, not campus IT load and not new nameplate owned by Oracle. It is kept separate from the ENGIE Texas renewable supply ceiling and is not an Oracle campus total. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.headline: ENGIE to match up to 568 MW for Oracle in Texas
rows.summary: ENGIE North America announced renewable supply agreements on 17 September 2026 to help supply up to 568 MW of wind electricity in ERCOT for Oracle's Texas operations. The plants are unnamed. The 568 MW figure is a matching ceiling, not campus IT, and it is not added to the RWE Panther Creek 433 MW VPPA. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.headline: Meta signs 144 MW Starling Solar matching PPA
rows.summary: Apex Clean Energy signed a power purchase agreement with Meta for exclusive rights to energy and renewable energy credits from the 144 MW Starling Solar project in Gonzales County, Texas, announced 16 September 2026. Commercial operation is expected in 2027. This row is renewable matching, not campus IT. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.headline: Williams placed Socrates South into service in late July 2026
rows.summary: Williams's Q2 2026 10-Q says Socrates South was placed into service in late July 2026. The customer is Meta's affiliate Sidecat LLC. This 200 MW is on-site generation and is not added to Meta's IT.

rows.headline: Williams says Socrates North remains under construction
rows.summary: Williams's Q2 2026 10-Q says Socrates North remains under construction. The customer is Meta's affiliate Sidecat LLC. This 200 MW is on-site generation and is not added to Meta's IT.

rows.headline: Meta pins Prometheus at 1 GW of AI cluster capacity
rows.summary: Engineering at Meta pinned the next AI cluster, Prometheus, at 1 gigawatt on 29 September 2025. The 1,000 MW figure is AI cluster capacity across multiple data center buildings. Meta's 9 January 2026 nuclear newsroom places the Prometheus supercluster in New Albany, Ohio. This row is not behind-the-meter generation and not IT load. Socrates South and Socrates North stay on their own rows. Oklo and Vistra nuclear matching stay on their existing rows. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.headline: Crusoe designs 672 MW critical IT for Microsoft at Abilene campus 2
rows.summary: Site prep and plan-review building records that don't name Crusoe are not construction.

rows.headline: 900 MW of on-site generation announced at Abilene campus 2
rows.summary: On 27 March 2026 Crusoe said the new Microsoft campus in Abilene includes 900 megawatts of new on-site power generation and a 900 MW on-site power plant. The only construction line in that release is land clearing and site preparation for the campus, which is not plant construction. Status is announced. Energized MW and COD are empty. The 672 MW critical IT row is separate and unchanged.

rows.project: Cheyenne Business Parkway critical IT lease
rows.headline: CoreWeave leases 88 MW critical IT at Related Digital Cheyenne
rows.summary: Related Digital broke ground on 7 October 2025 on a Cheyenne campus designed for up to 302 MW of critical IT. CoreWeave is the anchor tenant on a long-term lease for 88 MW of critical IT in the first building. This row is the 88 MW lease. The 302 MW campus design is not the pin. Black Hills Energy is the utility path, not a second megawatt figure. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.headline: Galaxy delivers Helios Phase I at 133 MW critical IT to CoreWeave
rows.summary: Galaxy said on 6 July 2026 that Helios Phase I in West Texas was delivered on schedule: about 200 MW gross and 133 MW of critical IT load to CoreWeave, with rent commencement in the second quarter of 2026. The campus is in Afton, Dickens County. This row is the 133 MW critical IT figure. The 526 MW commitment across Phases I through III is not this pin, and the 200 MW gross figure is not substituted for critical IT. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.project: Kansas City AI factory, initial phase
rows.headline: Lambda plans a 24 MW first phase in Kansas City
rows.summary: Lambda said on 28 October 2025 it plans to reuse a 2009 facility in Kansas City, Missouri, as sole tenant. The site is expected to launch with 24 MW of capacity, with a stated potential to scale past 100 MW. This row is the 24 MW phase only. The larger scale-up is not pinned, and Plano is not on this row. The customer is unnamed in the primary. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.headline: IREN contracts Microsoft 200 MW critical IT at Childress
rows.summary: IREN announced on 3 November 2025 a multi-year agreement with Microsoft to deploy NVIDIA GB300 clusters in liquid-cooled halls under construction at Childress, Texas. The GPUs, in four phases through 2026 (Horizon 1-4), collectively provide 200 MW of critical IT load. This row is that 200 MW. The 750 MW campus shell is not this pin. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.project: Project Matador phase one facility power
rows.headline: TensorWave leases 222 MW facility power at Fermi Matador
rows.summary: Fermi announced on 10 August 2026 a binding lease between Fermi Campus 1 LLC and TensorWave TEX1, LLC at Project Matador in Carson County, Texas. Phase one is 222 MW of total facility power, with phased delivery beginning in the second half of 2027. Expansion rights that would take the partnership above 650 MW are not this pin. The lease has customary conditions, including receipt of project guaranties and financing. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.headline: Nebius pins Highridge at a 260 MW initial phase
rows.summary: Nebius describes an owned AI factory at Highridge Business Park in Butler Township, Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania, at Interstate 81 and Gordon Mountain Road. The project page states an initial phase of 260 MW, with 260 MW of power delivery expected by October 2027. This row is that 260 MW phase only. The 1.2 GW full-buildout design, the later 660 MW and 1,000+ MW steps, and other Nebius US up-to designs including Independence and New Jersey are not on this row. The page does not carry a dateline; the phase figure was public in July 2026. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.project: Cameron County AI campus first phase
rows.headline: Fluidstack begins Cameron County first phase, planned up to 1.5 GW
rows.summary: Fluidstack said on 21 September 2026 that construction has begun on the first phase of its AI data center campus in Cameron County, Texas, planned to support up to 1.5 GW. Do not add this campus to the separate Fluidstack campuses at Lake Mariner, Abernathy, Barber Lake, River Bend, or Meridian Arc. Those five campuses are not summed with this one. This row is not the Anthropic Texas and New York plan. The page does not publish a parcel. The page says construction has begun, and no commercial operation date is given.

rows.project: Lebanon Facility (Boone County bridge BTM gas)
rows.headline: Life Cycle Power proposes 134 MW bridge gas for Meta Orla in Lebanon
rows.summary: Life Cycle Power proposes up to 134 MW of temporary natural-gas generators as bridge power solely for Meta's Orla LLC data center in Lebanon, Boone County, until permanent utility interconnection. The 20 February 2026 application (011-50087-00094) places the plant on West SR 32, next to Orla, also on West SR 32, and specifies 65 Caterpillar G3516H engines. IDEM treats LCP and Orla as a combined source for NSR and Title V, with separate permits (Orla T011-50034-00093, LCP 011-50087-00094). A public hearing is set for August 2026. This row is behind-the-meter generation, not IT load, and it is not the Fluidstack Meridian Arc campus in Sullivan County. The pin is the application coordinate on West SR 32. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.headline: PUCN conditionally approves 218 MW Peru Ridge bridge gas
rows.summary: PR RNO Property Owner 1, LLC, a Fleet Data Centers affiliate of Tract Capital, applied under PUCN docket 26-04027 to build the Peru Ridge Self-Generation Project, a temporary 218 MW natural-gas plant on private land in Storey County at the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center near Peru Drive. The primary docket page is the application. A 17 September 2026 conditional approval is secondary only (NVBEX and Nevada Current), and it remains subject to Nevada Division of Environmental Protection and Storey County permits. The plant is a two to three year bridge until NV Energy can serve the site. Construction is planned for early 2027. This row is behind-the-meter generation, not IT load, and it is not the South Valley 144 MW plant. The pin is Peru Drive in the industrial center, not a surveyed parcel corner. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.project: South Valley Temporary Power Generation Facility
rows.headline: PUCN conditionally approves 144 MW South Valley bridge gas
rows.summary: SV RNO Property Owner 1 LLC, a Fleet Data Centers affiliate of Tract Capital, applied under PUCN docket 26-04026 to build the South Valley Temporary Power Generation Facility, a temporary 144 MW natural-gas plant on private land in Storey County. The primary docket page is the application. A 17 September 2026 conditional approval is secondary only (NVBEX and Nevada Current), and it remains subject to Nevada Division of Environmental Protection and Storey County permits. The plant is a two to three year bridge until NV Energy can serve the site. Construction is planned for early 2027. This row is behind-the-meter generation, not IT load, and it is not the Peru Ridge 218 MW plant. The pin is the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center corridor south of Peru Drive, near the Lyon County line, not a surveyed parcel corner. Energized MW and days to COD are empty.

rows.project: PowerConneX II New Albany Energy Center
rows.headline: EdgeConneX started PowerConneX II in November 2025
rows.summary: EdgeConneX says construction started in November 2025. The only figure is up to 216 MW, so this row does not count.

rows.headline: Core Scientific lists 262 MW critical IT at Denton
rows.summary: Core Scientific Exhibit 99.2 lists Denton, Texas at 262 MW critical IT capacity contracted with CoreWeave. The filing says 132 MW were billable as of March 2026, which is not an energized figure. Energized MW and COD are empty. Grid capacity on the same line is not on this row. Do not add this site to the 1,300 MW Core Scientific row.

rows.headline: Core Scientific lists 30 MW critical IT at Dalton 1
rows.summary: Dalton 1 is 30 MW critical IT. Exhibit 99.2 says work has commenced, so this row counts. Dalton 4 is a separate row. Energized MW and COD are empty. Do not add this site to the 1,300 MW Core Scientific row.

rows.headline: Core Scientific lists 145 MW critical IT at Dalton 4
rows.summary: Dalton 4 will feature a 145 MW data center and is a greenfield development.

rows.headline: Core Scientific lists 70 MW critical IT at Muskogee
rows.summary: Core Scientific Exhibit 99.2 lists Muskogee, Oklahoma at 70 MW critical IT capacity contracted with CoreWeave. Status is construction from the filing. Energized MW and COD are empty. Grid capacity on the same line is not on this row. Do not add this site to the 1,300 MW Core Scientific row.

rows.headline: Core Scientific lists 65 MW critical IT at Marble
rows.summary: Core Scientific Exhibit 99.2 lists Marble, North Carolina at 65 MW critical IT capacity contracted with CoreWeave. Status is construction from the filing. Energized MW and COD are empty. Grid capacity on the same line is not on this row. Do not add this site to the 1,300 MW Core Scientific row.

rows.headline: Core Scientific lists 16.5 MW critical IT at Austin
rows.summary: Core Scientific Exhibit 99.2 lists Austin, Texas at 16.5 MW critical IT capacity contracted with CoreWeave. The filing says the Austin campus was completed in 2024, so status is operational. Energized MW and COD are empty because the filing does not state delivered MW. Do not add this site to the 1,300 MW Core Scientific row.

rows.headline: TCEQ review lists about 6,000 MW at Matador
rows.summary: A TCEQ technical review says the project's nominal generation capacity will be approximately 6,000 MW, solely onsite. Status is announced. The permit is not construction. Energized MW and COD are empty. No map pin: the filing does not give a site coordinate. Do not add this plant to the TensorWave 222 MW facility row.

rows.project: GW Ranch Energy Center gas plant
rows.headline: Air permit lists 5,000 MW at GW Ranch
rows.summary: The air permit technical review says Pacifico GW LLC proposes 35 natural gas-fired simple-cycle turbines at the GW Ranch Energy Center in Pecos County, with a nominal output of 5,000 megawatts. The plant is described as off-grid. This is not an Amazon IT row. Status is announced. Energized MW and COD are empty. No map pin: the filing does not give a site coordinate.

rows.headline: PUCT study lists a 265.5 MW large load at Goodnight One
rows.summary: A PUCT and ERCOT study describes the net metering arrangement between GOODNIT1 and the 265.5 MW large load. This is utility load for Crusoe One, on hold, and announced. It is not IT capacity and it is not the 265.5 MW wind nameplate in the same report. Energized MW and COD are empty. No map pin: the study does not give a site coordinate in the cited line.

rows.headline: PUCT study lists a 260 MW data center load at Goodnight Two
rows.summary: A PUCT and ERCOT study describes a new 260 MW artificial-intelligence data-center complex. This is utility load for Ensign and Crusoe Two, on hold, and announced. It is not IT capacity and it is not a wind nameplate. Energized MW and COD are empty. No map pin: the study does not give a site coordinate in the cited line.

rows.headline: Independence plans for IPL to deliver 200 MW
rows.summary: The City of Independence deck says IPL is to deliver 200 MW in late Q3 2026. This is utility delivery, on hold, and announced. It is not IT capacity and it is not the 1.2 GW design held separately. Energized MW and COD are empty. No map pin: the deck does not give a site coordinate in the cited line.

rows.headline: Google supports about 96 MW of uprates at Vogtle and Hatch
rows.summary: Georgia Power says that under the agreement, which is subject to approval by the Georgia PSC, Google will support uprates on Georgia Power's owned portion of the nuclear units at Plants Vogtle and Hatch that will allow the facilities to add approximately 96 megawatts of new capacity to the electric grid to serve Georgia Power customers. Google will subscribe to the NU-1 tariff and receive the zero-emission credits for that uprate output. The agreement is included in filings in dockets 44280 and 56002 made at the Georgia PSC. Those filings also include a new Nuclear Uprate (NU-1) tariff structure. The pin is approximate and is not a campus. Energized MW and COD are empty.

rows.counterparty: Zerra DC, Australian Data Centres, and Macquarie Capital
rows.project: Western Downs Digital Park first-stage lease
rows.headline: Anthropic signs a first-stage lease in Western Downs
rows.summary: Dexus says a consortium of Zerra DC, Australian Data Centres, and Macquarie Capital has entered into a lease for the first stage of a campus in the Western Downs region of Queensland with an Australian subsidiary of Anthropic, subject to customary approvals. The release states no megawatts. The pin is approximate and is not an exact site. Energized MW and COD are empty.

rows.headline: DTE states 1,000 MW for the Google data center in Van Buren Township
rows.summary: On 1 Oct 2026 the Michigan Public Service Commission approved special contracts between DTE Electric Co. and Google LLC to provide electricity for a data center in Van Buren Township, Wayne County (Case U-22058). The release states a contract length of 20 years and a minimum billing demand of 80%. It says, according to DTE Electric, service is expected to begin in December 2027, with a maximum load by December 2028. Those dates stay note-only. The MPSC release does not state a megawatt size. DTE's 28 Sep 2026 Form 8-K states an executed 1 GW agreement with Google. The 1,000 MW stored on this row is company-stated (DTE 8-K), not MPSC-stated. This row stays utility load and does not count. The same MPSC release says Google will pay for up to 1,600 MW of renewable energy and 480 MW of storage. Those up-to figures stay note-only and are not stored as capacity. No map pin: the release does not give a site coordinate. Energized MW and COD are empty.

rows.headline: AIB signs a binding 50 MW IT lease with Nebius at CLT-01
rows.summary: On 30 Sep 2026 AIB Data Centers Inc. announced a binding 12-year lease with Nebius for 50 MW of critical IT at CLT-01 in South Carolina. The lease is supported by AIB's 15-year Electric Service Agreement for 65 MW of utility load at the site. The 50 MW sits inside the 65 MW. Never add the 50 MW IT lease to the 65 MW utility load. The utility is unnamed in the primary. The primary has no construction-began language, so this contracted IT row does not count. Two halls are forward-looking. AIB portfolio figures of about 120 MW of contracted power and about 505 MW under evaluation are not this row. Do not sum this row with nebius-highridge-pa-phase-260 or nebius-independence-200. Energized MW and COD are empty. No map pin: the release does not name a city or a site coordinate.

rows.project: Point Beach Nuclear Plant output subscription
rows.headline: Oracle announces a Point Beach nuclear output subscription
rows.summary: On 2 Oct 2026 Oracle announced a subscription to a portion of existing Point Beach Nuclear Plant output with We Energies, tied to Project Lighthouse and Port Washington. This is offtake from an existing plant. It is not new plant capacity and it is not IT. Capacity is empty because the primary does not state a megawatt figure. Public Service Commission of Wisconsin approval is pending. This row is separate from stargate-port-washington-wisconsin-vantage, the 902 MW IT row, and is never added to that IT row. The portion sits inside We Energies' existing purchase path. Energized MW and COD are empty. No map pin: the announcement does not give a site coordinate.
